correctness.rationale: The exact group law yields three commutator coordinates. Counting determinant constraints fixes outer fibers; a rank-one-versus-zero split of the last-coordinate linear map yields the three numbers. The exceptional q² sextuples and free central variables give precisely q^8 extra at the identity. Full direct-group enumeration at q=2 and q=3 and separate GF(4) field arithmetic reproduce the formulas. The proof is symbolic and works for every prime-power q; experiments alone do not prove this.

value.rationale: Group-commutator word maps and single-commutator width are canonical invariants; exact target-refined distributions are more informative than commuting probabilities. UT4 is the minimal class-three unitriangular case, revealing a uniform characteristic-free two-to-one central-vs-noncentral concentration plus an identity correction. This provides a complete natural arithmetic classification for all q, not an arbitrary small numeric slice.
